issue.title: Upd #243875

comment.body:
> Then we'll consider when that occurs. In content blocking, we only address things when there are real cases and we won't go overboard with theoretical situations unless there were further discussions about it.

I understand. Is there a way you could talk to ghajini about this so I don’t have to deal with what happened in the mentioned issue every time a site using adthrive’s anti-adblock is reported? As far as I can tell, they all use the same script, so they should always be added to both the scriptlet and allow rules when you see this URL being called: `ads.adthrive.com/abd/abd.js`.

issue.title: Upd #236328

comment.body:
There were some issues with HTML Filtering in Firefox:

- https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardBrowserExtension/issues/2249
- https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardBrowserExtension/issues/2646
- https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardBrowserExtension/issues/2826

so those rules are temporarily excluded on Firefox right now

https://github.com/AdguardTeam/FiltersCompiler/blob/29d7d955ba7b9108b2d7ac3f1ec59e96e4577d80/src/main/platforms-config.js#L765-L766

I guess it should be fine now for reported cases but I'm not sure.

---

issue.title: Upd #243875

comment.body:
> it would be nice if we could limit it to iOS (Free) users rather than all iOS users.

It's fine. As I said, for iOS users that can use advanced rules, they can already use the other 2 scriptlets and the `googlesyndication` XHR connection won't appear, so the exceptions don't affect them either.

issue.title: Upd #243875

comment.body: Unfortunately, we need the exception because not all AdGuard platforms support scriptlets or redirect rules. The allow rule is already limited to those platforms, although it would be nice if we could limit it to iOS (Free) users rather than all iOS users.

issue.title: Upd #243875

comment.body: I think it's not needed. The thing is if a platform can use scriptlets, the other 2 scriptlets already make `googlesyndication.com` XHR connection not appear.

issue.title: Upd #243875

comment.body:
> `#%#//scriptlet('set-cookie', '__adblocker', 'false') + #%#//scriptlet('prevent-xhr', 'ads.adthrive.com')` is not enough?

They work fine. I only added the extra scriptlet to make ghajini feel a little better about any possible privacy concerns. The extra scriptlet should prevent the sites from fetching `pagead2.googlesyndication.com`, but other than that, it doesn’t really do anything, as the other scriptlets already take care of the problem.

Enable AdGuard Home with the current AdGuard DNS filter. > 2. Open the affected URL. > 3. Scroll to the in-article display advertisement. > 4. The advertisement is loaded despite DNS filtering. > > ### Findings > The ad iframe uses rotating numbered hosts under `stg.wear.boohoonor.com`, including `0` through `9` prefixes observed in the page DOM. One observed example was `5.stg.wear.boohoonor.com`. > > DNS inspection showed the delivery chain using `sdi.html-load.com`. The current published AdGuard DNS filter did not contain rules for `boohoonor` or `html-load` when checked on 2026-10-11. A content-filter rule for `html-load.com` with a popup modifier exists elsewhere, but it does not stop this DNS-level subresource case. > > The following AdGuard Home user rules stop the advertisement: > > ``` > ||stg.wear.boohoonor.com^ > ||html-load.com^ > ``` > > Please consider adding suitable rules to the AdGuard DNS filter. The report concerns the attached banner and this rotating cloaked host family. No private network details are included. ### Screenshots

Yeah, please always give full details of which ones don't match, don't give the sample links piece-by-piece.

```
[-_a-zA-Z0-9][-_a-zA-Z0-9][-_a-zA-Z0-9][-_a-zA-Z0-9][-_a-zA-Z0-9][-_a-zA-Z0-9]?[-_a-zA-Z0-9]?[-_a-zA-Z0-9]?[-_a-zA-Z0-9]?[-_a-zA-Z0-9]?
```

comment.body:
I’m not sure I’ll be able to handle this with a single rule, as this is as specific as I can make it while still having it match.

`^https:\/\/[a-z]{3,}\.[a-z]{7,}\.com\/[a-z]{3,}-[a-z]{3,}\/[a-zA-Z0-9-_]{5,10}\.js$`

Unless make it wide and do something like this:
`^https:\/\/[a-z]{3,}\.[a-z]{7,}\.com\/[a-z]{3,}-[a-z]{3,}\/[a-zA-Z0-9-_]{5,}\.js$`

However, at that point, it might just be better to add chrome to the IOS rule.

comment.body: No, iOS rules are not meant for other platforms. iOS rules can exceed MV3 limitations. It's just their supported syntaxes are not the same as MV3. Each platform has different limitations: - iOS regexes don't have risks of memory exceed like in MV3, but they have limited syntaxes -> iOS regexes can still cause memory exceed in MV3. - MV3 regexes have more syntaxes but they have arbitrarily memory exceeded issues -> simple MV3 regexes can still be not available on iOS. Don't mix up the regexes of these 2 platforms together please. --- The current iOS regex in the PR also exceeds memory on MV3:

```javascript

},(result)=>console.log(result))
```

So the above non-broad regex should work fine.

### Issue URL (Social Widget) [https://fp3-siken.com/kakomon.php](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Ffp3-siken.com%2Fkakomon.php) ### Comment > > > Bug Report: Social share buttons are no longer blocked > > Description > > On the target website (reported in this issue), the social media share buttons are no longer blocked and remain visible. > > Conditions for Reproduction > > This issue occurs only when both of the following filters are added and enabled as Custom Filters (rather than enabling them from the app’s default filter list): > > • Japanese Filter (Full / Unoptimized): https://filters.adtidy.org/ios/filters/7.txt > • Social Media Filter (Full / Unoptimized): https://filters.adtidy.org/ios/filters/4.txt > > Notes on when the issue does NOT occur: > > • Adding other filters as custom filters does not trigger the issue. > • Default Social Media Filter + Custom Japanese Filter -> Works as expected. > • Custom Social Media Filter + Default Japanese Filter -> Works as expected. > • The issue strictly occurs when both are registered as custom filters. > > Screenshots / Guide to the Reproduction Page > > I have attached screenshots that show, step by step, how to navigate from the site’s top page to the page where the issue can be reproduced. Please refer to them to reach the affected page and confirm that the share buttons remain visible. > > Workaround > > Adding a user rule to hide the specific element temporarily resolves the issue. > Interestingly, adding the exact rule that should already be included in the Social Media Filter as a user rule also fixes it. This indicates that the rule itself works fine, but something within the filter combination is overriding or negating it. > > Possible Cause > > I suspect that a rule present in the full (unoptimized) version but removed in the optimized (built-in) version of one of these filters is interfering with the hiding of the share buttons. > Since adding filters with even more rules than the Japanese Filter (e.g., the Cookie Notices filter) does not reproduce the issue, I have concluded this is not caused by hitting the iOS Content Blocker rule limit. > > Why using “Optimized Filters” is not a solution > > I browse a massive number of websites for both work and personal use. Reporting broken sites caused by rules stripped during optimization defeats the purpose. As long as I am within the iOS rule limit, using full versions via custom filters should fundamentally work. > > Request > > Please investigate and fix the cause, or explain the root cause of this conflict. > I am happy to provide logs, screenshots, exported settings, or specific related rules if needed. The attached screenshots should make the reproduction steps clear, but please let me know before closing this as “Cannot reproduce”—I am fully willing to assist in confirming the reproduction steps. > > Additionally, the operator of this website runs several other websites using the exact same layout (listed below). Please refer to them to reach the affected page and confirm that the share buttons remain visible. > > Workaround > > Adding a user rule to hide the specific element temporarily resolves the issue. > Interestingly, adding the exact rule that should already be included in the Social Media Filter as a user rule also fixes it. This indicates that the rule itself works fine, but something within the filter combination is overriding or negating it. > > Possible Cause > > I suspect that a rule present in the full (unoptimized) version but removed in the optimized (built-in) version of one of these filters is interfering with the hiding of the share buttons. > Since adding filters with even more rules than the Japanese Filter (e.g., the Cookie Notices filter) does not reproduce the issue, I have concluded this is not caused by hitting the iOS Content Blocker rule limit. > > Why using “Optimized Filters” is not a solution > > I browse a massive number of websites for both work and personal use. Reporting broken sites caused by rules stripped during optimization defeats the purpose. As long as I am within the iOS rule limit, using full versions via custom filters should fundamentally work. > > Request > > Please investigate and fix the cause, or explain the root cause of this conflict. > I am happy to provide logs, screenshots, exported settings, or specific related rules if needed. The attached screenshots should make the reproduction steps clear, but please let me know before closing this as “Cannot reproduce”—I am fully willing to assist in confirming the reproduction steps. > > Additionally, the operator of this website runs several other websites using the exact same layout (listed below). comment.body:
I copied the pattern from the explorecams.com rules without a reason specific to this site.

The DNS case is handled by the scriptlet instead: `scriptlet('abort-on-stack-trace', 'btoa', 'redirectToSupportPage')`. I tested DNS with both checks forced to fail: the page stayed on `/server/index`, and after a click there was no wall.

So I've removed the redirect line and keep:
- the 2 scriptlets
- the `@@||ad-delivery.net/px.gif?` exception, limited to `ios, ext_android_cb, ext_safari`

issue.body:
# ATTENTION

> [!NOTE]  
> YouTube changes their detection scripts regularly. That means that sometime you can face the detection message.
> If all the following instructions do not work, please **email filters@adguard.com** or wait until any update is available. 

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use another adblocker in the same time because using another adblocker can delay/lags the YouTube loading (e.g., AdBlock Plus and AdBlock)[^1] OR interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use an userscript related to the bypassing YouTube detection message like [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing).
> Recently, YouTube anti-adblock script added infinite dummy advertisements to try to neutralize the userscript. ( [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing#264](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing/issues/264) )

> [!WARNING]
> Please check that there no another web browser extension that has adblocking feature is enabled on your web browser. It can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!IMPORTANT]  
> Saving memory feature of your web browser or sleep feature of your operating system can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.
> In this case, please re-enable AdGuard's filtering by toggling the protection toggle.
> Following the instructions can be needed.

### The instructions
1. Force to update the filters by clicking the reload button in AdGuard Browser Extension/AdGuard mobile or update tray menu in your system tray. [^2]
2. Reload the YouTube webpage without cache by pressing <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd> [^3].
3. Clear cache, cookies and site data of your web browser.
4. Re-open your web browser completely (checking your system monitor[^4] will be better).

[^1]: https://gitlab.com/adblockinc/ext/adblockplus/adblockplusui/-/issues/1576
[^2]: [AdGuard for Windows](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-windows/overview/#tray-menu); [AdGuard for Mac](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-mac/overview/#updates-check); 
[^3]: On macOS, <kbd>Command</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd>
[^4]: Task Manager on Windows, System Monitor on GNOME Shell, KDE System Guard on KDE Plasma or Activity Monitor on macOS. 


Previous issue https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/issues/198973

### Issue URL (Social Widget) [https://fp3-siken.com/kakomon.php](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Ffp3-siken.com%2Fkakomon.php) ### Comment > > > Bug Report: Social share buttons are no longer blocked > > Description > > On the target website (reported in this issue), the social media share buttons are no longer blocked and remain visible. > > Conditions for Reproduction > > This issue occurs only when both of the following filters are added and enabled as Custom Filters (rather than enabling them from the app’s default filter list): > > • Japanese Filter (Full / Unoptimized): https://filters.adtidy.org/ios/filters/7.txt > • Social Media Filter (Full / Unoptimized): https://filters.adtidy.org/ios/filters/4.txt > > Notes on when the issue does NOT occur: > > • Adding other filters as custom filters does not trigger the issue. > • Default Social Media Filter + Custom Japanese Filter -> Works as expected. > • Custom Social Media Filter + Default Japanese Filter -> Works as expected. > • The issue strictly occurs when both are registered as custom filters. > > Screenshots / Guide to the Reproduction Page > > I have attached screenshots that show, step by step, how to navigate from the site’s top page to the page where the issue can be reproduced. Please refer to them to reach the affected page and confirm that the share buttons remain visible. > > Workaround > > Adding a user rule to hide the specific element temporarily resolves the issue. > Interestingly, adding the exact rule that should already be included in the Social Media Filter as a user rule also fixes it. This indicates that the rule itself works fine, but something within the filter combination is overriding or negating it. > > Possible Cause > > I suspect that a rule present in the full (unoptimized) version but removed in the optimized (built-in) version of one of these filters is interfering with the hiding of the share buttons. > Since adding filters with even more rules than the Japanese Filter (e.g., the Cookie Notices filter) does not reproduce the issue, I have concluded this is not caused by hitting the iOS Content Blocker rule limit. > > Why using “Optimized Filters” is not a solution > > I browse a massive number of websites for both work and personal use. Reporting broken sites caused by rules stripped during optimization defeats the purpose. As long as I am within the iOS rule limit, using full versions via custom filters should fundamentally work. > > Request > > Please investigate and fix the cause, or explain the root cause of this conflict. > I am happy to provide logs, screenshots, exported settings, or specific related rules if needed. The attached screenshots should make the reproduction steps clear, but please let me know before closing this as “Cannot reproduce”—I am fully willing to assist in confirming the reproduction steps. > > Additionally, the operator of this website runs several other websites using the exact same layout (listed below). issue.body:
# ATTENTION

> [!NOTE]  
> YouTube changes their detection scripts regularly. That means that sometime you can face the detection message.
> If all the following instructions do not work, please **email filters@adguard.com** or wait until any update is available. 

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use another adblocker in the same time because using another adblocker can delay/lags the YouTube loading (e.g., AdBlock Plus and AdBlock)[^1] OR interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use an userscript related to the bypassing YouTube detection message like [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing).
> Recently, YouTube anti-adblock script added infinite dummy advertisements to try to neutralize the userscript. ( [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing#264](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing/issues/264) )

> [!WARNING]
> Please check that there no another web browser extension that has adblocking feature is enabled on your web browser. It can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!IMPORTANT]  
> Saving memory feature of your web browser or sleep feature of your operating system can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.
> In this case, please re-enable AdGuard's filtering by toggling the protection toggle.
> Following the instructions can be needed.

### The instructions
1. Force to update the filters by clicking the reload button in AdGuard Browser Extension/AdGuard mobile or update tray menu in your system tray. [^2]
2. Reload the YouTube webpage without cache by pressing <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd> [^3].
3. Clear cache, cookies and site data of your web browser.
4. Re-open your web browser completely (checking your system monitor[^4] will be better).

Please refer to them to reach the affected page and confirm that the share buttons remain visible. > > Workaround > > Adding a user rule to hide the specific element temporarily resolves the issue. > Interestingly, adding the exact rule that should already be included in the Social Media Filter as a user rule also fixes it. This indicates that the rule itself works fine, but something within the filter combination is overriding or negating it. > > Possible Cause > > I suspect that a rule present in the full (unoptimized) version but removed in the optimized (built-in) version of one of these filters is interfering with the hiding of the share buttons. > Since adding filters with even more rules than the Japanese Filter (e.g., the Cookie Notices filter) does not reproduce the issue, I have concluded this is not caused by hitting the iOS Content Blocker rule limit. > > Why using “Optimized Filters” is not a solution > > I browse a massive number of websites for both work and personal use. Reporting broken sites caused by rules stripped during optimization defeats the purpose. As long as I am within the iOS rule limit, using full versions via custom filters should fundamentally work. > > Request > > Please investigate and fix the cause, or explain the root cause of this conflict. > I am happy to provide logs, screenshots, exported settings, or specific related rules if needed. The attached screenshots should make the reproduction steps clear, but please let me know before closing this as “Cannot reproduce”—I am fully willing to assist in confirming the reproduction steps. > > Additionally, the operator of this website runs several other websites using the exact same layout (listed below). issue.body:
# ATTENTION

> [!NOTE]  
> YouTube changes their detection scripts regularly. That means that sometime you can face the detection message.
> If all the following instructions do not work, please **email filters@adguard.com** or wait until any update is available. 

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use another adblocker in the same time because using another adblocker can delay/lags the YouTube loading (e.g., AdBlock Plus and AdBlock)[^1] OR interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use an userscript related to the bypassing YouTube detection message like [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing).
> Recently, YouTube anti-adblock script added infinite dummy advertisements to try to neutralize the userscript. ( [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing#264](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing/issues/264) )

> [!WARNING]
> Please check that there no another web browser extension that has adblocking feature is enabled on your web browser. It can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!IMPORTANT]  
> Saving memory feature of your web browser or sleep feature of your operating system can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.
> In this case, please re-enable AdGuard's filtering by toggling the protection toggle.
> Following the instructions can be needed.

### The instructions
1. Force to update the filters by clicking the reload button in AdGuard Browser Extension/AdGuard mobile or update tray menu in your system tray. [^2]
2. Reload the YouTube webpage without cache by pressing <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd> [^3].
3. Clear cache, cookies and site data of your web browser.
4. Re-open your web browser completely (checking your system monitor[^4] will be better).

[^1]: https://gitlab.com/adblockinc/ext/adblockplus/adblockplusui/-/issues/1576
[^2]: [AdGuard for Windows](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-windows/overview/#tray-menu); [AdGuard for Mac](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-mac/overview/#updates-check); 
[^3]: On macOS, <kbd>Command</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd>
[^4]: Task Manager on Windows, System Monitor on GNOME Shell, KDE System Guard on KDE Plasma or Activity Monitor on macOS. 


Previous issue https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/issues/198973

Default settings (only AdGuard Base filter and AdGuard DNS filter) with HTTPS filtering works. @Alex-302 Figured out the setting, it's caused by enabling "Block third-party Authorization header".
The following rule works: ```adblock @@||cbsi.live.ott.irdeto.com/streaming/getckc^$stealth=3p-auth,domain=paramountplus.com|cbs.com ``` If I remove this rule, the video reports error 3301. Once I add this rule back, the video plays with no error 3301.

issue.body:
### Issue URL (Social Widget) [https://fp3-siken.com/kakomon.php](https://adguardteam.github.io/AnonymousRedirect/redirect.html?url=https%3A%2F%2Ffp3-siken.com%2Fkakomon.php) ### Comment > > > Bug Report: Social share buttons are no longer blocked > > Description > > On the target website (reported in this issue), the social media share buttons are no longer blocked and remain visible. > > Conditions for Reproduction > > This issue occurs only when both of the following filters are added and enabled as Custom Filters (rather than enabling them from the app’s default filter list): > > • Japanese Filter (Full / Unoptimized): https://filters.adtidy.org/ios/filters/7.txt > • Social Media Filter (Full / Unoptimized): https://filters.adtidy.org/ios/filters/4.txt > > Notes on when the issue does NOT occur: > > • Adding other filters as custom filters does not trigger the issue. > • Default Social Media Filter + Custom Japanese Filter -> Works as expected. > • Custom Social Media Filter + Default Japanese Filter -> Works as expected. > • The issue strictly occurs when both are registered as custom filters. > > Screenshots / Guide to the Reproduction Page > > I have attached screenshots that show, step by step, how to navigate from the site’s top page to the page where the issue can be reproduced. Please refer to them to reach the affected page and confirm that the share buttons remain visible. > > Workaround > > Adding a user rule to hide the specific element temporarily resolves the issue. > Interestingly, adding the exact rule that should already be included in the Social Media Filter as a user rule also fixes it. This indicates that the rule itself works fine, but something within the filter combination is overriding or negating it. > > Possible Cause > > I suspect that a rule present in the full (unoptimized) version but removed in the optimized (built-in) version of one of these filters is interfering with the hiding of the share buttons. > Since adding filters with even more rules than the Japanese Filter (e.g., the Cookie Notices filter) does not reproduce the issue, I have concluded this is not caused by hitting the iOS Content Blocker rule limit. > > Why using “Optimized Filters” is not a solution > > I browse a massive number of websites for both work and personal use. Reporting broken sites caused by rules stripped during optimization defeats the purpose. As long as I am within the iOS rule limit, using full versions via custom filters should fundamentally work. > > Request > > Please investigate and fix the cause, or explain the root cause of this conflict. > I am happy to provide logs, screenshots, exported settings, or specific related rules if needed. The attached screenshots should make the reproduction steps clear, but please let me know before closing this as “Cannot reproduce”—I am fully willing to assist in confirming the reproduction steps. > > Additionally, the operator of this website runs several other websites using the exact same layout (listed below). It would be greatly appreciated if these could be addressed as well. If I need to create separate issues for them, please let me know. > > Thanks. > ### Screenshots

issue.body:
# ATTENTION

> [!NOTE]  
> YouTube changes their detection scripts regularly. That means that sometime you can face the detection message.
> If all the following instructions do not work, please **email filters@adguard.com** or wait until any update is available. 

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use another adblocker in the same time because using another adblocker can delay/lags the YouTube loading (e.g., AdBlock Plus and AdBlock)[^1] OR interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use an userscript related to the bypassing YouTube detection message like [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing).
> Recently, YouTube anti-adblock script added infinite dummy advertisements to try to neutralize the userscript. ( [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing#264](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing/issues/264) )

> [!WARNING]
> Please check that there no another web browser extension that has adblocking feature is enabled on your web browser. It can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!IMPORTANT]  
> Saving memory feature of your web browser or sleep feature of your operating system can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.
> In this case, please re-enable AdGuard's filtering by toggling the protection toggle.
> Following the instructions can be needed.

### The instructions
1. Force to update the filters by clicking the reload button in AdGuard Browser Extension/AdGuard mobile or update tray menu in your system tray. [^2]
2. Reload the YouTube webpage without cache by pressing <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd> [^3].
3. Clear cache, cookies and site data of your web browser.
4. Re-open your web browser completely (checking your system monitor[^4] will be better).

[^1]: https://gitlab.com/adblockinc/ext/adblockplus/adblockplusui/-/issues/1576
[^2]: [AdGuard for Windows](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-windows/overview/#tray-menu); [AdGuard for Mac](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-mac/overview/#updates-check); 
[^3]: On macOS, <kbd>Command</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd>
[^4]: Task Manager on Windows, System Monitor on GNOME Shell, KDE System Guard on KDE Plasma or Activity Monitor on macOS.

labels.description: Website or app not working properly due to filtering

labels.name: A: Cannot reproduce
labels.description: Filters devs cannot reproduce this issue

issue.body:
# ATTENTION

> [!NOTE]  
> YouTube changes their detection scripts regularly. That means that sometime you can face the detection message.
> If all the following instructions do not work, please **email filters@adguard.com** or wait until any update is available. 

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use another adblocker in the same time because using another adblocker can delay/lags the YouTube loading (e.g., AdBlock Plus and AdBlock)[^1] OR interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use an userscript related to the bypassing YouTube detection message like [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing).
> Recently, YouTube anti-adblock script added infinite dummy advertisements to try to neutralize the userscript. ( [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing#264](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing/issues/264) )

> [!WARNING]
> Please check that there no another web browser extension that has adblocking feature is enabled on your web browser. It can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!IMPORTANT]  
> Saving memory feature of your web browser or sleep feature of your operating system can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.
> In this case, please re-enable AdGuard's filtering by toggling the protection toggle.
> Following the instructions can be needed.

### The instructions
1. Force to update the filters by clicking the reload button in AdGuard Browser Extension/AdGuard mobile or update tray menu in your system tray. [^2]
2. Reload the YouTube webpage without cache by pressing <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd> [^3].
3. Clear cache, cookies and site data of your web browser.
4. Re-open your web browser completely (checking your system monitor[^4] will be better).

[^1]: https://gitlab.com/adblockinc/ext/adblockplus/adblockplusui/-/issues/1576
[^2]: [AdGuard for Windows](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-windows/overview/#tray-menu); [AdGuard for Mac](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-mac/overview/#updates-check); 
[^3]: On macOS, <kbd>Command</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd>
[^4]: Task Manager on Windows, System Monitor on GNOME Shell, KDE System Guard on KDE Plasma or Activity Monitor on macOS. 


Previous issue https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/issues/198973

labels.name: T: Incorrect Blocking
labels.description: Website or app not working properly due to filtering

labels.name: A: Cannot reproduce
labels.description: Filters devs cannot reproduce this issue

issue.body:
# ATTENTION

> [!NOTE]  
> YouTube changes their detection scripts regularly. That means that sometime you can face the detection message.
> If all the following instructions do not work, please **email filters@adguard.com** or wait until any update is available. 

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use another adblocker in the same time because using another adblocker can delay/lags the YouTube loading (e.g., AdBlock Plus and AdBlock)[^1] OR interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use an userscript related to the bypassing YouTube detection message like [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing).
> Recently, YouTube anti-adblock script added infinite dummy advertisements to try to neutralize the userscript. ( [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing#264](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing/issues/264) )

> [!WARNING]
> Please check that there no another web browser extension that has adblocking feature is enabled on your web browser. It can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!IMPORTANT]  
> Saving memory feature of your web browser or sleep feature of your operating system can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.
> In this case, please re-enable AdGuard's filtering by toggling the protection toggle.
> Following the instructions can be needed.

### The instructions
1. Force to update the filters by clicking the reload button in AdGuard Browser Extension/AdGuard mobile or update tray menu in your system tray. [^2]
2. Reload the YouTube webpage without cache by pressing <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd> [^3].
3. Clear cache, cookies and site data of your web browser.
4. Re-open your web browser completely (checking your system monitor[^4] will be better).

[^1]: https://gitlab.com/adblockinc/ext/adblockplus/adblockplusui/-/issues/1576
[^2]: [AdGuard for Windows](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-windows/overview/#tray-menu); [AdGuard for Mac](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-mac/overview/#updates-check); 
[^3]: On macOS, <kbd>Command</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd>
[^4]: Task Manager on Windows, System Monitor on GNOME Shell, KDE System Guard on KDE Plasma or Activity Monitor on macOS. 


Previous issue https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/issues/198973

labels.name: A: Cannot reproduce
labels.description: Filters devs cannot reproduce this issue

issue.body:
# ATTENTION

> [!NOTE]  
> YouTube changes their detection scripts regularly. That means that sometime you can face the detection message.
> If all the following instructions do not work, please **email filters@adguard.com** or wait until any update is available. 

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use another adblocker in the same time because using another adblocker can delay/lags the YouTube loading (e.g., AdBlock Plus and AdBlock)[^1] OR interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!CAUTION] 
> Please do not use an userscript related to the bypassing YouTube detection message like [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing).
> Recently, YouTube anti-adblock script added infinite dummy advertisements to try to neutralize the userscript. ( [TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing#264](https://github.com/TheRealJoelmatic/RemoveAdblockThing/issues/264) )

> [!WARNING]
> Please check that there no another web browser extension that has adblocking feature is enabled on your web browser. It can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.

> [!IMPORTANT]  
> Saving memory feature of your web browser or sleep feature of your operating system can interfere AdGuard's filtering functionality.
> In this case, please re-enable AdGuard's filtering by toggling the protection toggle.
> Following the instructions can be needed.

### The instructions
1. Force to update the filters by clicking the reload button in AdGuard Browser Extension/AdGuard mobile or update tray menu in your system tray. [^2]
2. Reload the YouTube webpage without cache by pressing <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd> [^3].
3. Clear cache, cookies and site data of your web browser.
4. Re-open your web browser completely (checking your system monitor[^4] will be better).

[^1]: https://gitlab.com/adblockinc/ext/adblockplus/adblockplusui/-/issues/1576
[^2]: [AdGuard for Windows](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-windows/overview/#tray-menu); [AdGuard for Mac](https://adguard.com/kb/adguard-for-mac/overview/#updates-check); 
[^3]: On macOS, <kbd>Command</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>R</kbd>
[^4]: Task Manager on Windows, System Monitor on GNOME Shell, KDE System Guard on KDE Plasma or Activity Monitor on macOS. 


Previous issue https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardFilters/issues/198973
